Recording analysis

Select a local RRD, inspect its annotated fields, and analyze exact samples. Tables preserve native types and nanosecond clocks. No resampling or forward-fill is applied. state = null means an explicitly recorded null; an absent sample means the field was not acquired at that time. NaN and infinities remain distinct. Duplicate this notebook for a particular experiment and add cells using run, run.fields[path], and filtered_samples.

Your analysis

Add cells below. Useful starting points: 
# A typed table, including exact timestamps and explicit value state:
servo = run.samples("/mavlink/SERVO_OUTPUT_RAW/servo3_raw", timeline="mission")

# Keep real finite measurements only when appropriate for the calculation:
finite = servo.filter((pl.col("state") == "present") & pl.col("value").is_finite())

# Count events per second without inventing values between messages:
rates = servo.group_by((pl.col("time_s").floor()).alias("second")).len().sort("second")
For cross-message joins, choose a clock, an as-of direction, and a tolerance explicitly. Never interpret a sent command as an acknowledgment from the vehicle. For exact joins, use the integer *_ns columns rather than floating-point seconds.
